en: Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator using hot water bottles to keep premature babies warm in rural Philippine hospitals without electricity.
The Ifugao maintain muyong woodlots above their rice terraces to filter rainwater, prevent deadly landslides, and ensure a safe supply of irrigation water.
The Department of Health uses the Pinggang Pinoy visual plate guide to help Filipino students balance meals with local foods to prevent malnutrition.
Indigenous healers use crushed tawa-tawa plant leaves to help manage dengue fever symptoms by naturally supporting the body's platelet production.
The NDRRMC mandates the Duck, Cover, and Hold drill in all Philippine schools to protect students from falling debris during earthquakes.
The Kalinga bodong peace pact system resolves tribal disputes without violence, creating a physically safer environment for children to walk to school.
Republic Act 11106 declared Filipino Sign Language as the national sign language, ensuring deaf students have the legal right to accessible emergency communication.
The Local Government Code empowers barangay officials to regularly clear drainage canals, which prevents stagnant water and stops dengue-carrying mosquitoes from breeding.
T'boli weavers extract natural dyes from plants for their t'nalak cloth, avoiding the toxic skin rashes caused by synthetic chemical dyes.
In 1901, the colonial Bureau of Health introduced mandatory smallpox vaccinations in Manila, drastically reducing child mortality rates from this deadly virus.
The traditional Filipino practice of sun-drying fish like daing removes moisture, safely preserving the meat and preventing food poisoning during long travels.
National hero Jose Rizal advocated for proper waste disposal and clean water in Dapitan, significantly reducing the spread of waterborne diseases among locals.
